# Phase 1: Recon — Learn the Convention Before Touching Anything

Do this before drafting or editing any flavor-narrative deck README/
`theme_analysis.md`. Do not start writing prose yet — this phase is read-only.

## Read the reference decks

Read all three "Somebunny Is Having a Party" READMEs in full:
- [Baylen](../../../decks/Somebunny%20Is%20Having%20a%20Party/Baylen%20–%20Somebunny%20Brought%20the%20Whole%20Warren/README.md)
- [Finneas](../../../decks/Somebunny%20Is%20Having%20a%20Party/Finneas%20–%20Somebunny’s%20On%20the%20Menu/README.md)
- [Ms. Bumbleflower](../../../decks/Somebunny%20Is%20Having%20a%20Party/Ms.%20Bumbleflower%20–%20Somebunny%20Said%20I%20Do/README.md)

Also skim a "bare" README from a deck without a story (e.g. anything under
`decks/Cold-Blooded Monsters/`) for contrast — this shows what a README looks
like *before* this treatment is applied.

## The one hard rule (non-negotiable)

**Never justify or write a card's placement by what it *does* in-game.**
Use only the card's literal name, title, flavor text, or art. This applies to
your *reasoning* while proposing a spot for a card, not just the final prose
— if your justification mentions mill, tutoring, ramp, counters, wipes,
card draw, etc., it is a rule violation even if that word never makes it
into the shipped sentence. This was violated once mid-project and drew a
strong negative reaction from the user — treat it as strict and
non-negotiable, not a soft style preference. See
[readme-editorial-rules memory](../../../../../memories/repo/readme-editorial-rules.md)
if present.

## Shared narrative skeleton (extract this from the reference decks)

- A happy/positive opening that establishes the premise and the "host"
  character (the commander).
- A slow, escalating middle that stays upbeat — do not front-load negativity;
  paragraphs before the pivot must read positive even when the underlying
  card is a downside card.
- One clearly marked pivot sentence, with an explicit contrast word
  (but/although/until/soon), that turns the story from positive to negative.
- A back half that follows real cause-and-effect (pain → escalation →
  suppression → consequence), not just a list of bad things in random order.
- A punchy closing tagline.

## Next phase

Once you've internalized the above, move to card-to-beat planning: see the
`deck-flavor-readme-card-mapping` skill. For the file's headers/sections
(title, metadata table, mosaic placement) rather than the story itself, see
the separate `deck-flavor-readme-layout` skill — that's a mechanical,
checker-enforced concern distinct from the narrative craft above.
